lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1721 — your name was the three dots

*"why are there 3 dots on the top left corner"* — that is your character's name.

⚠⚠⚠ THE NAME ROW GIVES ITS TWO SIDES OPPOSITE INSTRUCTIONS:

    name:         { flexShrink: 1 }   → gives up width
    nameRowRight: { flexShrink: 0 }   → never gives up width

Which is correct while the right side holds BADGES — "◆ 58 PWR", "Rust (16/16)".
Those are short, the name has room, and nobody notices the asymmetry. But the
DOWNED-DOG COUNTDOWN was stacked into that same column, and it is not a badge, it
is a sentence: "Rust ⏳ 24h — feed to save". `numberOfLines={1}` means it cannot
wrap and `flexShrink: 0` means it will not yield, so it took the row, and the name
— the only thing left that shrinks — collapsed to a bare ellipsis.

For as long as Rust was bleeding out, your character had no name on your own
screen. The warning that shipped to save the dog is what erased the player. Your
screenshot shows it exactly as the arithmetic predicts: line one `...` and
`◆ 58 PWR`, line two the countdown.

⚠⚠ THE FIX IS THE SHAPE. The sentence gets a full-width row of its own — the same
shape the golem line has used since OTA-145 — so the corner holds only badges
again. Its 200pt cap goes with it: that was a right-aligned chip's cap, and on its
own row a 16-character dog name must not be able to clip "feed to save" off the
one warning in the game with a deadline attached. The healthy-dog badge stays
where it is; it was never the problem.

⚠ THEN A FLOOR, so the CLASS cannot come back. `minWidth: 64` on the name means
whatever anyone stacks in that column next leaves a truncated name rather than
three dots. I left the right column at `flexShrink: 0` deliberately — making it
shrink would truncate the POWER rating instead, which is the worse trade.

An instrument checks that nothing in the badge column renders a sentence. It
caught my own first cut: I scanned raw source and it flagged the comment
explaining the fix, because that comment quotes the string it moved. A scanner
that cannot tell its subject from its own notes measures nothing, so it strips
comments now.

⚠ ON THE HEALTH ITSELF: your HP row is correct — 43/47, and the numbers agree
with the feed. What is missing next to it is a BAR. The enemy card has one and
your card does not, which is most of why the panel reads as broken at a glance
even when the numbers are fine. That is a design call rather than a defect, so I
have not added one; say the word and it is a small change.
